## Broadcasted Integer Operations {.unnumbered}


### Description

The <code>bc.i()</code> method
performs broadcasted integer operations on 2 numeric or logical arrays. <br>
<br>
Please note that these operations will treat the input as (53 or 32 bit) integers,
and will efficiently truncate using <code>trunc2int53()</code> when necessary. <br>
Therefore, something like <code>bc.i(1, 1.5, "==")</code> returns <code>TRUE</code>,
because <code>trunc(1.5)</code> equals <code>1</code>. <br>
<br>
For regular relational operators, see [bc.rel](bc.rel.qmd). <br>
<br>
<br>



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>bc.i(x, y, op, ...)

## S4 method for signature 'ANY'
bc.i(x, y, op)

trunc2int53(x)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="x">x</code>, <code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
conformable vectors/arrays of type logical or numeric.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="op">op</code></td>
<td>
a single string, giving the operator. <br>
Supported integer operators: gcd, %%, %/%, pmin, pmax. <br>
Supported relational operators: ==, !=, &lt;, &gt;, &lt;=, &gt;=. <br>
The &quot;gcd&quot; operator performs the &quot;Greatest Common Divisor&quot; operation,
using the Euclidean algorithm.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="...">...</code></td>
<td>
further arguments passed to or from methods. <br> <br>
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

For <code>trunc2int53()</code>: <br>
Base 'R' supports 53 bit integers from <code>-1 * (2^53 - 1)</code> to <code>2^53 - 1</code>,
which thus range from approximately <code>-9</code> quadrillion to <code>+9</code> quadrillion. <br>
<code>trunc2int53()</code> will truncate a numeric vector (like <code>trunc()</code>),
and replace all values above <code>2^53 - 1</code> with <code>Inf</code>,
and values below <code>-1 * (2^53 - 1)</code> with <code>-Inf</code>. <br>
<br>

For integer operators: <br>
A numeric (<code>double</code> or <code>integer</code>, depending on the situation) array of whole numbers,
as a result of the broadcasted arithmetic operation. <br>
Values outside of the 53 bit integer range will be returned as <code>-Inf</code> or <code>Inf</code>,
as in <code>trunc2int53()</code>,
as an extra protection against integer precision loss. <br>
<br>
For relational operators: <br>
A logical array as a result of the broadcasted integer relational comparison. <br>
The relational operators efficiently truncate the input during broadcasting using <code>trunc2int53()</code>. <br>
<br>

### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>"}
library("broadcast")

x.dim <- c(4:2)
x.len <- prod(x.dim)
x.data <- sample(c(NA, 1.1:1000.1), x.len, TRUE)
x <- array(x.data, x.dim)
y <- array(1:50, c(4,1,1))

bc.i(x, y, "%%")
bc.i(x, y, "%/%")
bc.i(x, y, "gcd") # greatest common divisor

bc.i(x, y, "==")
bc.i(x, y, "!=")
bc.i(x, y, "<")
bc.i(x, y, ">")
bc.i(x, y, "<=")
bc.i(x, y, ">=")



```
